author: agent-core team
description: Read-only access to a self-hosted HealthQuery personal health dashboard: sync status, activity, sleep, vitals and body views, timelines, import batches, settings, read-only data queries, reports, and health questions. Nothing here can change anything.

setup.instructions:
Connect Agent Core to a self-hosted HealthQuery install.

1. Run HealthQuery and confirm its API is reachable: GET {base_url}/api/health returns 200.
2. Use the HealthQuery read token, not the ingest token. The read token is HEALTHQUERY_READ_TOKEN in HealthQuery's api container environment.
3. Add a connection to this service:
   - Service address (base_url): the HealthQuery service root only, e.g. https://health.example.com or http://healthquery-api:3136 if Agent Core shares the Docker network. Do NOT include /api/health or /api/reports; each action appends its own path.
   - read_token: the HealthQuery read token. It is sent as a Bearer token.

This service intentionally does not expose the ingest webhook or the settings update endpoint. Agent Core blocks private and loopback addresses unless the address is on the allowed private addresses list in Settings > Security.

fields.name: read_token
fields.description: HealthQuery read token (HEALTHQUERY_READ_TOKEN). Sent as a Bearer token.

actions.name: get_health_check
actions.description: Check HealthQuery API liveness and database connectivity.

actions.name: get_health_status
actions.description: Return HealthQuery's sync status, last sync time, and how many records it holds.

actions.name: get_health_overview
actions.description: Return HealthQuery overview dashboard data and latest health snapshot.

actions.name: get_health_summary
actions.description: Return the summary view used by HealthQuery's overview dashboard.

actions.name: get_health_activity
actions.description: Return daily activity summaries and workout data.

actions.name: get_health_sleep
actions.description: Return sleep sessions, stages, and sleep summary data.

actions.name: get_health_vitals
actions.description: Return vitals such as heart rate, resting heart rate, HRV, SpO2, temperature, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and glucose when present.

actions.name: get_health_body
actions.description: Return body metrics such as weight, body fat, height, lean mass, bone mass, and body water when present.

actions.name: get_health_timeline
actions.description: Return recent timeline events across HealthQuery categories.

days.description: Lookback window in days. HealthQuery defaults to 14.

actions.name: get_health_batches
actions.description: Return summaries of the most recent data imports.

limit.description: Maximum number of recent batches to return. HealthQuery defaults to 10.

actions.name: get_health_config
actions.description: Return the non-secret settings, including report windows and whether the question assistant is set up.

actions.name: execute_health_query
actions.description: Run a read-only SQL SELECT through HealthQuery's safety check. HealthQuery caps the size of the result.

sql.description: A single read-only SELECT statement accepted by HealthQuery's SQL guard.

actions.name: generate_doctor_visit_report
actions.description: Produce HealthQuery's doctor-visit report for an optional date range.

start_date.description: Optional inclusive start date as YYYY-MM-DD.

end_date.description: Optional inclusive end date as YYYY-MM-DD.

actions.name: ask_health_question
actions.description: Ask HealthQuery's optional health assistant a question about an optional date range.

question.description: Question to ask about the stored health data.

start_date.description: Optional inclusive start date as YYYY-MM-DD.

end_date.description: Optional inclusive end date as YYYY-MM-DD.
